answer_1.quote: We introduce a new task of Neutral Multi-News Summarization (NEUS) to mitigate media framing bias by providing a neutral summary of articles, along with the dataset ALLSIDES and a set of metrics.
answer_1.outputs: neutral summary of articles from multiple sources

answer_2.quote: We use three metrics to evaluate summaries from different dimensions. For framing bias, we propose a polarity-based metric... For evaluating whether the summaries retain salient information, we adopt commonly used information recall metrics... In addition, we use a hallucination metric to evaluate if the generations contain any unfaithful hallucinatory information...

answer_4.quote: We conduct A/B testing where the annotators are given two generated articles about an issue, one with a higher Arousal sum score and the other with a lower score. Then, annotators are asked to select the more biased article summary.
answer_4.guideline: We also provide examples and the definition of framing bias for a better understanding of the task. We obtain three annotations each for 50 samples and select those with the majority of votes.
